title: Fundamental groups of a dense open surject
statement:
Let $V$ be a connected normal Noetherian scheme, let
$k:V'\hookrightarrow V$ be a dense open immersion, and let $\bar v$ be a
geometric point of $V'$, with the fundamental groups of
[def-galois-fibre-functor].

1. (*Geometric surjectivity.*) The map
   $\pi_1(V',\bar v)\to\pi_1(V,\bar v)$ induced by pullback of finite
   etale covers is surjective. Equivalently, a connected finite etale
   cover of $V$ stays connected over $V'$.
2. (*Weil groups.*) Let $V_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme
   whose base change $V=V_0\times_{k_0}k$ is connected and normal, let
   $V'_0\subseteq V_0$ be a dense open, and put
   $V'=V'_0\times_{k_0}k$. Then the induced map of Weil groups
   $W(V'_0)\to W(V_0)$ of [def-wf-weil-group] commutes with the degree
   maps, restricts on the geometric subgroups to the surjection of (1),
   and is surjective.
3. (*Lisse sheaves extend uniquely.*) For every lisse sheaf
   $\mathcal N$ on $V$ (at every finite coefficient level in the convention of
   [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and for lisse $\Qlb$-sheaves
   formed from compatible finite-level $\mathcal O_E$-models by
   inverting $\ell$ and extending coefficients to $\Qlb$, where
   $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite) the adjunction unit
   $\mathcal N\to k_*k^*\mathcal N$ is an isomorphism.
4. (*Restriction on curves.*) Let $U_0$ be a curve in the sense of
   [d-real-setup] and $k:U'_0\hookrightarrow U_0$ a nonempty open.
   Pullback $k^*$ from lisse Weil sheaves on $U_0$ to lisse Weil sheaves
   on $U'_0$ is fully faithful, and it carries irreducible objects (no
   lisse subsheaf other than $0$ and itself) to irreducible objects. The
   same holds for lisse $\Qlb$-sheaves on the geometric curves
   $U'\hookrightarrow U$.
5. (*Constructibility.*) If $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ is a nonempty
   open in a curve $C_0$ of [d-real-setup] and $\mathcal F$ is lisse on
   $U_0$, then the middle extension $j_*\mathcal F$ of
   [def-wf-middle-extension] is constructible at every finite
   coefficient level.

proof.text: *Step 0 ($V$ is integral).* The geometric point $\bar v$ of $V'$ makes $V'$ and $V$ nonempty. Apply clause (2) of [rem-pc-regular-normal] to the normal Noetherian $V$: its irreducible components are a finite disjoint family of open-and-closed normal integral subschemes covering $V$. Nonemptiness gives at least one component; if there were two or more, one component and the union of the others would disconnect $V$. Thus there is exactly one and $V$ is integral. Below we use the same argument only for nonempty connected normal Noetherian schemes. We do not use clause (3), whose nonemptiness hypothesis is now explicit.

source.place: Properties, Lemma \ref{lemma-normal-Noetherian} (Stacks Tag `033M`); the zero-component case is excluded by the geometric point

proof.text: *(1a).* Let $W\to V$ be a nonempty connected finite etale cover. Its image is open (etale) and closed (finite) and nonempty, so $W\to V$ is surjective since $V$ is connected. The scheme $W$ is Noetherian, being finite over $V$, so [lem-fin-etale-normal-components] makes it a finite disjoint union of open-and-closed normal integral schemes; connectedness makes $W$ integral. Its open subscheme $W\prime:=W\times_VV\prime$ is nonempty by surjectivity and $V\prime\ne\varnothing$, and a nonempty open of an integral scheme is irreducible and therefore connected. This proves the connected-cover formulation.

source.place: Proof, paragraph (1), first paragraph (the unit Step 4 argument)

proof.text: *(1b).* For the group formulation, note first that $V\prime$ is connected: apply the first paragraph to the connected finite etale cover $W=V$ (or note that $V\prime$ is a nonempty open of the integral $V$ of Step 0). Thus [thm-galois-fundamental] and [lem-fet-galois-category] apply to $V\prime$. Pullback is compatible with the fibre functors at $\bar v$, and [thm-galois-fundamental] gives the continuous homomorphism $\pi_1(V\prime,\bar v)\to\pi_1(V,\bar v)$ whose action on the fibre of $W$ is the action through this map. Its image $H$ is compact and hence closed in the profinite group $G:=\pi_1(V,\bar v)$. If $H\ne G$, [lem-wf-profinite-closed-subgroup-intersection-open] gives a proper open subgroup $H\subseteq U\subsetneq G$. By the open-subgroup/connected-cover correspondence [cor-galois-open-subgroups], $U$ is the stabilizer of a point of the fibre of a connected finite etale cover $P\to V$; equivalently, the fibre is the transitive $G$-set $G/U$. Since $H\subseteq U$ and $[G:U]\ge2$, the induced $\pi_1(V\prime)$-action fixes the coset $U$ and is not transitive. The base-change clause of [thm-galois-fundamental] identifies this with the fibre of $P\times_VV\prime$, while [lem-fet-galois-category] and [lem-galois-transitive] imply that a connected cover has transitive fibre; hence this pullback is disconnected, contradicting the first paragraph. Therefore $H=G$, proving surjectivity.

source.place: Proof, paragraph (1), fibre-functor and proper-open-subgroup argument; the separator is supplied by the cited Mathlib leaf

proof.text: *(2).* The projection $V=V_0\times_{k_0}\operatorname{Spec}k\to V_0$ is open by [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open]. Hence the inverse image $V\prime$ of the dense open $V\prime_0$ is dense in $V$: a nonempty open $O\subseteq V$ missing $V\prime$ would have a nonempty open image missing $V\prime_0$. Apply (1) to $V\prime\subseteq V$, and choose $\bar v$ in $V\prime$. By Step 0, $V$ is integral, so its nonempty open $V\prime=V\prime_0\times_{k_0}k$ is irreducible and hence connected. Since $k$ is algebraically closed, [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure] makes $V_0$ and $V\prime_0$ geometrically connected. This is the hypothesis of [def-wf-weil-group] and [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence] for both schemes. The morphism $V\prime_0\to V_0$ induces a map of arithmetic fundamental groups over $\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$, hence a map of the fibre products $W(-)=\pi_1(-,\bar v)\times_{\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)}\langle\Phi\rangle$ in [def-wf-fundamental-representation] that is the identity on $\langle\Phi\rangle$; this is compatibility with the degree maps in [def-wf-weil-group]. By [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence], the kernels are the geometric groups and the induced map between them is the surjection from (1). For $w\in W(V_0)$ of degree $n$, choose $w\prime\in W(V\prime_0)$ of degree $n$ using the same exact sequence. Then $w\bar w\prime^{-1}$ lies in $\pi_1(V)$, so lift it by (1) to $g\in\pi_1(V\prime)$; the product $gw\prime$ maps to $w$. Thus the Weil-group map is degree-compatible, restricts to the geometric surjection, and is surjective.

*(3).* Work first at a finite coefficient level; finite locally constant modules are as in [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Evaluate the unit on an affine etale $T\to V$. Such $T$ is Noetherian, so [lem-fin-etale-normal-components] decomposes it into finitely many open-and-closed normal integral components $T_i$. The inverse image $T\prime_i:=T_i\times_VV\prime$ is a nonempty dense open because the image of $T_i$ is a nonempty open of the integral $V$. Choose a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T\prime_i$. By the finite-coefficient equivalence [cor-galois-lisse-representations], sections of a lisse sheaf over connected $T_i$ identify with the invariants $\mathcal N_{\bar t}^{\pi_1(T_i,\bar t)}$, while sections over $T\prime_i$ identify with $\mathcal N_{\bar t}^{\pi_1(T\prime_i,\bar t)}$; restriction is inclusion of invariants. Applying (1) to $T\prime_i\subseteq T_i$ makes the two group images in $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal N_{\bar t})$ equal, so the invariants agree. The unit is therefore an isomorphism on every component and hence on $T$. For a lisse $\mathcal O_E$-model, apply these natural unit isomorphisms at every finite level. Their inverses commute with transition maps because the units do, so they give inverse morphisms of the inverse systems. Inverting $\ell$ and extending scalars to $\Qlb$ preserves these inverse identities, giving the stated lisse $\Qlb$ assertion.

*(4).* By [d-real-setup], $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$ is nonempty, connected, smooth and of finite type over $k$. It is normal by [lem-sc-smooth-normal] and Noetherian, so Step 0 makes it integral. Hence $U\prime=U\prime_0\times_{k_0}k$ is a nonempty open of $U$, so it is irreducible and connected. Since $U\prime_0$ is open in $U_0$, it is smooth, separated, of finite type and of pure dimension one, so it is again a curve of [d-real-setup]. As a nonempty open of the irreducible $U_0$, it is dense. Moreover $U$ and $U\prime$ share a geometric generic point. By [prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence] on $U_0$ and $U\prime_0$, lisse Weil sheaves are representations of their Weil groups on the generic stalk and pullback corresponds to restriction along $W(U\prime_0)\to W(U_0)$, because the generic stalk and the pulled-back fundamental representation are unchanged. This map is surjective by (2), since [d-real-setup] gives nonempty connected smooth geometric curves and [lem-sc-smooth-normal] gives their normality. A surjective group map yields equality of equivariant Hom spaces and of stable subspaces, so restriction is fully faithful and preserves irreducibility under the representation equivalence. The geometric $\Qlb$ version is the same argument using [cor-galois-lisse-representations] and (1).

*(5).* By [d-real-setup], $C_0$ is nonempty, smooth and of finite type over $k_0$, with connected geometric base change. The surjective projection from that connected base change shows that $C_0$ is connected. Its Noetherianity follows from finite type over a field, and [lem-sc-smooth-normal] gives normality. Clause (2) of [rem-pc-regular-normal], with nonemptiness and connectedness as in Step 0, now makes $C_0$ integral. The nonempty open $U_0$ is again a smooth curve and hence normal by [lem-sc-smooth-normal]. At each finite coefficient level $\mathcal F$ is finite locally constant, so [lem-fin-normal-open-lisse-image] applies and gives constructibility of the ordinary direct image, which is the middle extension in the statement.
